text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.47% today as oil prices softened and the broader energy sector faced headwinds from shifting market dynamics. U.S. crude dropped to $89.53 per barrel, and a major Wall Street narrative shifted away from refinery stocks—which had been among the year's best performers—suggesting investors are rotating out of energy positions. The stock has been volatile over the past week, losing about 4% from its mid-November high, partly reflecting this sector rotation.

The collapse of climate negotiations at COP31, which failed to restrict fossil fuels, could have been expected to support energy stocks, but instead the market appears focused on the unwinding of the refinery boom and uncertainty around Middle East supply disruptions (Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities, Iranian tensions) that have so far failed to sustainably lift crude prices higher.
